I have been farming these 6 mu for 25 years. I never went to school, but I know this land. Last year my wheat gave me about 500 kilos per mu, and the maize gave about 600 kilos per mu. This year I will do about the same — no reason to change what works.

For wheat, I sow in October, right after I rotary-till the field. I buy the improved wheat seed from the shop in town — about 30 jin per mu, which is roughly 15 kilos. Before sowing, I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, that is 50 kilos of the 15-15-15 type. That gives me some nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium all at once. Then when the wheat turns green in spring, I top-dress with urea — about half a bag per mu, around 25 kilos. Some years I add a little more if the plants look yellow. I would rather put on a bit too much than risk a thin harvest. A bad year means my family loses money; wasting a little fertilizer is just a cost I accept. For irrigation, I water three times: once before winter to help the seedlings survive, once at jointing when the stems shoot up, and once when the grain is filling. I have a well, so I can irrigate when I need to. For chemicals, I spray herbicide once after sowing, then insecticide twice, and fungicide once if the weather gets humid — that is four times total. My neighbor Lao Wang does about the same, and his wheat always looks good, so I copy him.

For maize, I plant it right after the wheat comes out in June. There is no time to plough deep — I either no-till or just scratch the surface. I plant hybrid maize seed, about one and a half packages per mu, roughly 1.5 kilos. At sowing, I put down 40 kilos of compound fertilizer per mu. Then when the plants are knee-high, I spread another 20 kilos of urea per mu. Maize needs water at the big trumpet stage and when it tassels, so I irrigate twice, three times if the summer is very dry. I spray herbicide once and insecticide twice — the corn borer comes every year, so I do not skip that. My cousin has a large farm and he uses machines to spray, but I do it by hand with a backpack sprayer.

My whole farm is 6 mu, so wheat gets all 6 mu in winter and maize gets all 6 mu in summer. Some money comes from my son working off-farm, so I can afford the inputs, but I still watch every yuan. I cannot afford a bad harvest.
